finding.claim: Unauthenticated SQL injection in /search: the q query parameter is interpolated into a LIKE string literal via an f-string, allowing a UNION-based read of any table in shop.db, including sqlite_master.
finding.source: app.py:11 request.args.get("q", "") — attacker-controlled query string on an unauthenticated route
finding.sink: app.py:12 db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") — string-interpolated SQL executed via sqlite3

trace.note: term read from request query string, no validation
f-string interpolation into LIKE literal, no parameter binding
db.execute runs the interpolated SQL via sqlite3
jsonify(rows) returns result set to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No escaping, allowlist, or length check on the path. No authentication or authorization on the route. Sibling routes use ? placeholders (app.py:18, app.py:25) so the flaw is local to this line. sqlite3 rejects stacked statements, so impact is read-only via UNION. Reachability depends on the unknown bind address: app.py has no app.run() or bind config; under flask run's loopback default the triage downgrade to MEDIUM would apply, while a public bind keeps HIGH. Reproduction was derived from code reading and not executed.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:11 reads q with no validation; app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL string with no parameter binding, escaping, or allowlist; the route at app.py:9-10 has no auth decorator or middleware. The only other files in the directory are .claude/skills/*.md and no auth or WSGI wrapper exists. Sqlite3's single-statement restriction limits the attack to a read-only UNION, which the claim already states.
verdict.reason: The trace matches app.py:11-13: q is read unvalidated at line 11, interpolated into the SQL at line 12 and executed with db.execute, and the rows are returned by jsonify at line 13, with no guard between them and no auth on the /search route (app.py:9-10). Reachability depends on the deployment bind address, which affects severity (HIGH vs MEDIUM) but not whether the flaw exists.
